title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning the Disposition of Seized Property by the Court That First Seized It and the Court Executing Priority Claims

articles.content_en: 1. During the process of enforcement, the court that first attaches, impounds, or freezes (hereinafter referred to as attachment) the property shall be responsible for disposing of the attached property. However, if a creditor's claim that has entered the enforcement proceedings of another court holds a security interest or priority right with a prior ranking on the attached property (such creditor's claim hereinafter referred to as priority claim), and more than 60 days have elapsed since the date of the first attachment, and the first-attachment court has not yet issued an auction announcement or commenced a sale procedure for the attached property, the enforcement court for the priority claim may request that the attached property be transferred to it for enforcement.

2. Where the enforcement court for the priority claim requests the first-attachment court to transfer the attached property for enforcement, it shall issue a consultation letter for transfer of enforcement, together with the effective legal instrument confirming the priority claim and a case description.
The first-attachment court shall, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the consultation letter for transfer of enforcement from the enforcement court for the priority claim, issue a letter of transfer of enforcement, transfer the attached property to the enforcement court for the priority claim for enforcement, and notify the parties.
The letter of transfer of enforcement shall state the matters such as the transfer of the attached property for enforcement and the relevant information on the first-attachment claim.

3. After the property is transferred for enforcement, when the enforcement court for the priority claim disposes of or continues to attach the property, it may handle the relevant formalities by presenting the letter of transfer of enforcement from the first-attachment court.
After the enforcement court for the priority claim converts the transferred property into money, it shall distribute the proceeds in accordance with the order of payment prescribed by law and inform the first-attachment court of the relevant circumstances.
If the first-attachment claim has not yet been confirmed by an effective legal instrument, the corresponding share shall be reserved in accordance with the ranking of the first-attachment claim for payment.

4. Where a dispute arises between the first-attachment court and the enforcement court for the priority claim concerning the transfer of the attached property, the courts may report the matter step by step to their common superior court to designate the enforcement court for the property.
If the common superior court, taking into account the specific circumstances of the case such as the stage of litigation in which the first-attachment claim is situated, the type and location of the attached property, and the relationship between the amount of each claim and the value of the attached property, considers that enforcement by the first-attachment court is more appropriate, it may also decide that the first-attachment court shall continue enforcement, but shall urge it to dispose of the attached property within a specified period.
This is issued in reply.

We have received your consultation letter for transfer of enforcement (××××) …… No. On (year) (month) (day), our court attached (or impounded or froze) …… (specify the property attached, hereinafter referred to as the attached property). Given that the creditor in your enforcement case (××××) …… No. enjoys a security interest (priority right) with a prior ranking on the attached property, now, in accordance with the provisions of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Relating to the First-Attachment Court and the Enforcement Court for Priority Claims in Disposing of Attached Property and at your court's request, we hereby transfer the above-mentioned attached property to your court for enforcement. Subsequent work such as continuation of attachment, release of attachment, conversion into money, and distribution of the property shall be handled by your court, and our court shall no longer be responsible.
